TOCTOU-proof containment for POSIX local drivers.

String-based checks ("resolve, compare, then operate") always leave a check-use gap: the filesystem can change between the comparison and the operation. This module removes the gap by making resolution and opening the same act. Every component of a path is opened with openat through a held parent file descriptor, so the descriptor you end up holding was obtained through a chain of verified parents. There is no later step to redirect.

Rules enforced by the walk:

  • openat is only ever called with a single plain component. .., ., / and empty components never reach a syscall: .. is resolved lexically with clamping at the root, and anything that would leave the root raises before any descriptor is opened.
  • Every openat carries O_NOFOLLOW, so a symlink fails loudly with ELOOP instead of being followed silently.
  • Following happens only deliberately: on ELOOP the target is read with readlinkat (one level, like std/symlinks), absolute targets are refused outright, and relative targets are spliced into the remaining walk which restarts from the root descriptor. A link budget of 40 bounds cycles. A symlink is therefore followed if and only if its resolved target stays inside the attached drive.
  • The root itself is canonicalized at construction, because on macOS even /tmp is a symlink; comparing resolved candidates against an unresolved root would reject everything legitimate.

Two entry points exist because some operations act on the link itself: resolving the final component unconditionally would make delete(link) remove the link's target and break readLink. openSecure resolves everything (data operations); openSecureParent walks all but the last component and returns (parentFd, basename) (link operations, creates, deletes, renames).

POSIX-only. On other platforms the same procedure names fall back to the previous lexical check (normalizedPath plus a separator-boundary prefix comparison), documented here as weaker: it closes the prefix-confusion hole but cannot close symlink or TOCTOU holes without openat.

Imports

core

Types

DirEntry = tuple[name: string, isDir: bool, size: int64, mtime: times.Time]
SandboxError = object of StorageError

Raised when a path escapes the driver root or a symlink cannot be resolved inside it. A subtype of StorageError, so existing except StorageError handlers are unaffected.

(SecureRoot itself lives in core, next to the driver types that carry it, to avoid an import cycle.)

Procs

proc atomicWriteSecure(root: SecureRoot; relpath, content: string; mode: Mode) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError, CatchableError, StorageError],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Write content atomically: tmp file in the same directory plus renameat, so a crash mid-write never corrupts the target. Parents are created first, then the parent is (re-)resolved through the walk, so every descriptor in play was verified. 
proc checkLexicalContained(root: SecureRoot; relpath: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Refuse relpath unless it lexically names something under the root. Used where the target need not exist (symlink creation): existence is irrelevant to the question being asked, which is purely "does this name stay inside". Absolute inputs must name the root itself or something under it; anything else raises exactly like the walk would. 
proc closeSecureRoot(r: var SecureRoot) {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Release the held root descriptor. Drivers live for process lifetime, so calling this is optional; it exists for embedding and tests. 
proc commitTemp(dirFd: cint; tmp, base: string) {....raises: [StorageError],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Atomically rename tmp over base in the held dirFd, cleaning up the temp file when the rename fails. 
proc copyDirSecure(root: SecureRoot; srcRel, dstRel: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError, CatchableError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Recursively copy a directory, including empty directories. Symlinked files resolve transparently when contained; symlinked directories are recreated as links only when their target resolves inside the drive, otherwise the copy fails closed rather than pulling outside content in. 
proc copyFileSecure(root: SecureRoot; srcRel, dstRel: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError, CatchableError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Copy file content fd-to-fd. A symlinked source is followed transparently when (and only when) its target resolves inside the drive — the walk enforces that, so outside content can never be pulled in. This preserves the previous observable behaviour for the valid case. 
proc createFileIn(dirFd: cint; base: string; mode = Mode(0o000000000666)): cint {.
    ...raises: [StorageError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Open base in the held dirFd for writing, creating or truncating, never following a symlink. Callers own the descriptor. 
proc ensureDirsSecure(root: SecureRoot; relpath: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
mkdir -p through verified parents. Existing components are fine (EEXIST is not an error); the final component is included, so callers pass the directory itself, not the file. 
proc ensureParentSecure(root: SecureRoot; relpath: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Ensure the parent directory of relpath exists, creating missing levels through verified parents. 
proc fstatFd(fd: cint): Stat {....raises: [StorageError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
fstat a held descriptor, raising on failure. 
proc fullMtime(st: Stat): times.Time {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Full-precision modification time. The second-granularity st_mtime accessor truncates sub-second precision, which breaks >= comparisons against getTime() taken just before an operation. 
proc listDirFd(dirFd: cint): seq[DirEntry] {....raises: [StorageError], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Enumerate a verified-open directory without touching path strings: fdopendir takes ownership, so hand it a duplicate and close the stream. The duplicate shares the file offset with the original, so rewind to 0 first — otherwise a second enumeration of the same descriptor starts at EOF and spuriously reports an empty directory. 
proc listSecure(root: SecureRoot; relpath: string; recursive: bool): seq[
    tuple[rel: string, st: Stat]] {....raises: [SandboxError, StorageError,
    CatchableError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Enumerate (relative path, lstat) pairs without any path string reaching the kernel after the initial walk. Symlinks appear as themselves (lstat semantics); outside-pointing links are listed but their targets are never traversed.

lstat without following the final component: true for symlinks themselves, false when absent, never raising for either.

proc openSecureParent(root: SecureRoot; relpath: string): tuple[dirFd: cint,

Walk all but the last component and return (parentFd, basename). The final component is never resolved, so link-acting operations (delete, readLink, renames) act on the link itself, never its target.

Open a driver root: create it if missing (matching newLocalDriver behaviour), canonicalize it fully, then hold it open as a directory descriptor. Everything descended from here starts from this descriptor, never from a re-parsed string.

proc removeSecure(root: SecureRoot; relpath: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError, CatchableError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Remove a file, symlink, or empty directory. Operates on the name itself (never resolves the final component), so deleting a link removes the link. A non-empty directory fails, matching delete semantics. A missing path is a silent no-op, matching delete idempotency. 
proc removeTreeSecure(root: SecureRoot; relpath: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError, CatchableError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Recursively delete a directory tree. Enumeration is fd-based; symlinked directories are listed but their targets are never traversed, and each removal names its entry through a held parent descriptor. 
proc renameSecure(root: SecureRoot; srcRel, dstRel: string) {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError, CatchableError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Move a file or directory with renameat. Both sides are parent-walked; a symlink is moved as a link (rename never follows), so no content crosses the boundary in either direction. 
proc searchSecure(root: SecureRoot; pattern: string): seq[string] {.
    ...raises: [SandboxError, StorageError, CatchableError], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Glob match over fd-enumerated relative paths. The pattern is split into segments and each segment is matched with fnmatch (no flags needed: segments never contain /), which mirrors walkPattern component semantics for the documented uses (*.txt, sub/*.log).

template sandboxPassthrough(op: string; path: string; body: untyped): untyped
Run body, letting SandboxError through unwrapped (so its "Path traversal detected: ..." message stays byte-identical for callers that assert on it) while wrapping anything else with operation context.
